text:
Jack H: Heads-up — we need ND40rs capacity in westeurope for the recommender service. Target: 6 nodes (24 GPUs) starting 2024-07-10 for a performance validation run. Subscription: sub-REDACTED-9a3f. Can infra kick off quota + capacity reservation request? Also need NSG port review (10250, 22, 443) and subnet size check.

Maria L: Created support case with Azure Support. Case #210456789 — https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/CaseBlade/overview/210456789. I asked them to bundle ND40rs quota, regional core quota, and a capacity reservation request in the same ticket. ETA initial response 48-72h. :eyes:

Priya K: Thanks Maria. Please request accelerated networking enablement and increase NIC limit per vNet (we hit NIC exhaustion last time). Also explicitly ask for regional vCPU quota bump — ND40rs maps into their vCPU quota model and Azure sometimes rejects SKU requests if core quota is low.

Dave R: Quick preflight checklist for the ticket: 1) SKU quota (ND40rs / ND40rs_v2 if available) 2) regional core quota increase (westeurope) 3) NIC/vNet limits and subnet size 4) capacity reservation (compute reservation ID request) 5) NSG/ports signoff 6) cost center + business justification doc. I can own NSG and peering changes once quota is confirmed.

Jack H: Budget note — estimate ~ $XXk/month for a 6-node reserved pool. Cost centre: ENG-INFRA-OPS. Please attach this to the case and highlight this is for a paid PoC with an enterprise customer (helps prioritization).

Azure Support Bot: Case 210456789 updated: Microsoft Support requested subscription-level verification and a capacity justification attachment. Please upload the requested docs in the case attachments.

Maria L: Uploaded the justification doc (performance test plan, node counts, expected traffic profile, runbook). I also added the preferred start date (2024-07-10) and a fallback region suggestion. Azure also linked a compute request intake form: https://aka.ms/compute-request-form — filled the high-level parts, left technical details to us.

Priya K: For capacity reservation — do we want a single-region reservation (westeurope) or primary + failover (westeurope primary, northeurope failover)? Recommend primary WEurope + NorthEU fallback. Also, please ask Azure for any required subscription limits (like accelerated networking opt-ins) that block ND40rs provisioning.

Dave R: Fallback options if Azure declines full reservation: 1) provision a smaller on-demand fleet in norwayeast for smoke runs, 2) reduce concurrency by tuning sequence length / KV cache to lower required GPUs, 3) use mixed SKUs (ND40rs + smaller NDv2) until reservation approved. I'll draft those options into the case.

Jack H: Can someone add billing contact (billing@redwood.ai) and exec sponsor (cto@redwood.ai) to the Azure case? Azure often requires billing contact for quota approval on large requests.

Maria L: Added both contacts and added a note requesting expedited handling due to customer timeline. I also pinged our Microsoft TAM and asked for a quick check-in. :pray:

Priya K: Once we get approval I'll open a runbook PR for the smoke test and a small terraform change to create the capacity-reservation resource. Example snippet to attach to the case (for reference):
```
resource "azurerm_capacity_reservation_group" "rrg" {
  name                = "redwood-rec-reservations"
  location            = "westeurope"
  resource_group_name = "rg-infra-prod"
}
```

Dave R: I'll monitor the case and post updates here. If we don't hear back in 72h ping me and I'll escalate with the TAM. Also tagging @Priya K to remind to prepare the runbook PR.

Jack H: Thanks all — appreciate the quick turn. Will standby for Azure reply and smoke test schedule.
